## Overview

`floraR` is an R package for accessing, analyzing, and curating taxonomic and distributional data from the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) platform, maintained by the [Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden](https://www.gov.br/jbrj/pt-br). It offers a comprehensive interface to the FFB [IPT data portal](https://ipt.jbrj.gov.br/jbrj/resource?r=lista_especies_flora_brasil): downloading, parsing, filtering, and exploring versioned Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) checklist data — from browsing by taxonomic, geographic, or trait criteria to resolving your own species name lists against it.

Beyond data retrieval, `floraR` also assists taxonomic experts contributing to FFB by simplifying the integration of new species names and records from global biodiversity repositories such as IPNI, REFLORA, and GBIF.

## Flora e Funga do Brasil

Brazil harbors the richest plant, algal, and fungal diversity in the world ([BFG 2022](https://doi.org/10.1002/tax.12640)). The checklist that documents it began in 2008 as the *Lista de Espécies da Flora do Brasil*, evolved into [Flora do Brasil 2020](http://doi.org/10.47871/jbrj2021004) to meet Brazil's Global Strategy for Plant Conservation commitments, and — after incorporating fungi — became [Flora e Funga do Brasil](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/).

For each accepted name, FFB records nomenclatural status, taxonomic classification, geographic distribution, endemism, life form, habitat, and vegetation type — a validated taxonomic backbone assembled collaboratively by hundreds of taxonomists and published as versioned Darwin Core Archives.

## Package Description

Package: `floraR`
Type: R Package
Version: 1.0.0

Author: Domingos Cardoso ([\@DBOSlab](https://github.com/DBOSlab) [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7072-2656))

Maintainer: Domingos Cardoso (<domingoscardoso@jbrj.gov.br>)

### Features

- Comprehensive interface to the Flora e Funga do Brasil IPT data portal
- Version tracking and offline-capable parsing of downloaded DwC-A datasets
- Checklist filtering by taxonomic, geographic, and trait-based criteria
- Exact and fuzzy (Levenshtein-distance) name resolution against the checklist
- Taxonomic hierarchy traversal at any rank, from class down to species
- Tools for data curation and integration with global biodiversity repositories
- Tidyverse-integrated workflows throughout

- Suggesting or developing new features (please open an issue for discussion first)
